headline: Paraguay Sovereign Bonds and Country Risk Deteriorate Following Political Crisis
summary: Following the political crisis and the resignation of President Santiago Peña amid the collapse of Ueno Bank, Paraguay's country risk rose 5.1% to 144 basis points, and sovereign bonds fell to their lowest level since June 2025.
why: Political instability and banking sector distress severely impair sovereign credit risk perceptions and depress international bond valuations.

impacts.name: Paraguay
impacts.why: Political turmoil and bank collapse directly drive up sovereign bond yields and country risk spreads.
